newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian newspaper warns Israel against attack.
newsitem.headline: Syrian newspaper warns Israel against attack.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday of preparing for war against Damascus but said any attack would "not be a mere picnic".

Tishreen daily said Israeli military exercises in the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in 1967, were "part of Israel's declared war against the peace process. They are conducted at the orders of Netanyahu."
"It is clear that the direct objectives of the Israeli military games are to provoke Syria, heighten tension and prepare for a possible aggression if that was necessary," Tishreen said.
But it added: "Any aggression against Syria will certainly not be a mere picnic as some Israeli officials think. It will bleed the aggressor."
Israeli forces ended military excercises in the Golan on Tuesday in which planes, tanks and artillery were used. The manoeuvres came amid mounting tension with Syria.
Syria redeployed some 12,000 troops in Lebanon in September, moving some units to within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights.
But in Washington a State Department spokesman said on Tuesday the United States saw no cause for concern over the recent Syrian troop movements which caused anxiety in Israel.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara on Tuesday denied any intention by Damascus to attack Israel and said the Jewish state was making such allegations to evade peace.

Tishreen said Arabs and the world understood the policies of Netanyahu and would "hold him responsible for any reckless adventure that he might make. They will not stand hands folded against such an action."

"It is better for Israel's leaders to return to the peace process and abandon the policy of occupation, settlements, expansion and aggression and to commit themselves to the world community's will because all have interest in peace."
Israel and Syria have held sporadic peace talks since 1991 but with little progress.

Syria and Arab states condemn Netanyahu for refusing to trade occupied Arab lands for peace. Damascus said it would not return to negotiations until Netanyahu approved the principle of withdrawal from the Golan.
